dw-main-gold.ddm.audit_06_campaign_servi.description:
* SQLMesh Model: Campaign Serving Old Creatives Audit
 * 
 * Original Procedure: ddm.audit_06_campaign_serving_old_creatives
 * Converted from Redshift stored procedure to SQLMesh model
 * 
 * Description: Feature audit to detect campaigns serving impressions on creatives
 *              that were unweighted (weight = 0) 1-30 days ago. This identifies
 *              cases where old/unweighted creatives are still being served, which
 *              should not happen.
 * 
 *              Logic:
 *              1. Find creative groups set to weight = 0, updated 1-30 days ago
 *              2. Check if impressions were served on those creatives in the last day,
 *                 but after the update_time + 1 hour
 *              3. FAIL if impressions found, PASS otherwise
 * 
 * Author: Converted from original procedure
 * Converted to SQLMesh: 2026-01-16

* SQLMesh Model: Prospecting Conversion Block Logic Audit
 * 
 * Original Procedure: ddm.audit_111_prospecting_conversion_block_logic

 * 
 * Description: Feature audit to ensure prospecting campaigns are properly blocking
 *              FPA (First-Party Audience) conversions. Some prospecting campaigns
 *              should be blocking FPA audiences for the advertiser. This audit cycles
 *              through advertisers and checks prospecting campaigns to ensure there

dw-main-gold.ddm.audit_112_franchise_eve.description:
* SQLMesh Model: Franchise Events Audit
 * 
 * Original Procedure: ddm.audit_112_franchise_events
 * Converted from PostgreSQL stored procedure to SQLMesh model
 * 
 * Description: Feature audit on franchise events.
 * 
 *              Web pixel events containing a hid (hotel ID) are treated as franchise events
 *              and are first sent to a franchise Kafka topic. These events then trigger the
 *              creation of guidv2 and/or conversion events.
 *              - If only hid is present, a guidv2 or conversion event is generated for each
 *                advertiser linked to that hotel.
 *              - If both hid and fid (franchise ID) are present, a single guidv2 or conversion
 *                event is generated only for the advertiser associated with the given fid.
 * 
 *              This audit checks that the correct number of guidv2 or conversion events are
 *              created based on these rules by comparing actual page views vs average page views
 *              per advertiser/hotel combination.
 * 
 * Author: Converted from original procedure
 * Converted to SQLMesh: 2026-01-23
 *
 * guid_log.query_map is a STRUCT; hid/fid read via $.key_value.list (see ber_stg.waypoints__base).

 *     EXPENSIVE LOGIC, WE ARE GOING WITH THIS SIMPLIFIED VERSION WHICH HAS SOME ERRORS, ESPECIALLY 
 *     FOR LONG RUNNING CAMPAIGNS. BUT HONESTLY, IF YOU ARE CARRYING AN IP FOR MONTHS, IT IS SAFE

One row per day per signup_platform_id (the platform the advertiser signed up on, 1=PTV/2=Express — from dim_advertiser current record; unmatched advertisers default to 1/PTV). Each measure (total_spend, impressions, visits, conversions, order_value) is pivoted into exhaustive platform (1=PTV, 2=Express, other) and product (1=PTV, 2=Select, other) breakout columns from fct_campaign_group, plus a grand-total column. A daily reconciliation audit asserts *_total matches fct_campaign_group. Grain: day x signup_platform_id.

dw-main-silver.identity.crm_audience.description: Daily snapshot mapping CRM audience uploads to household IPs from the identity graph for downstream targeting. Each daily run appends a new asofdate partition. Reads public.identity_graph directly as the single source of truth: graph_inputs holds the (id, household_id, id_type) projection for HEM_SHA256 and PHONE_SHA256 lookups, graph_outputs holds the household -> IP projection, and CRM email and phone uploads are unioned into a single crm_inputs hash list. The match join is on hash value alone (no id_type constraint) — see graph_inputs comment for rationale. Output: (audience_upload_id, advertiser_id, ip, source_id_type, asofdate); source_id_type carries the identity-graph id_type for the matched id (20 = HEM_SHA256, 60 = PHONE_SHA256).

dw-main-silver.identity.crm_audience_inc.description: Current, non-shared household IPv4 addresses for CRM-matched audiences — the crm_audience match restricted to inclusion-eligible IPs. Matches advertiser CRM email/phone uploads (data sources 4, 45) to the identity graph by hash, then maps the matched households to their IPv4s. Both legs are restricted to non-shared (is_shared = FALSE), currently-active (end_time IS NULL) linkages: the hash -> household match (id_type 20/60) and the household -> IPv4 output (id_type 30). FULL model: fully rebuilt each run against the latest graph_version; asofdate stamped to the build date. Output: (audience_upload_id, advertiser_id, ip, source_id_type, asofdate); source_id_type carries the identity-graph id_type for the matched id (20 = HEM_SHA256, 60 = PHONE_SHA256).

dw-main-silver.identity.crm_match_rate.description: Daily CRM audience match rate against the identity graph for both hashed email (HEM_SHA256, id_type 20) and hashed phone (PHONE_SHA256, id_type 60). Each daily run appends a new asofdate partition. Per audience_upload_id we emit one row with HEM totals/matches/rate and phone totals/matches/rate. Coverage uses DS63 semantics: a hash is counted as matched only if it resolves through the graph to a non-shared, currently-active IPv4 (i.e. it would appear in crm_audience_inclusion) — not merely present in the graph (the older DS47-style presence check). Reads public.identity_graph directly as the single source of truth: graph_ids holds the non-shared/current hash -> household leg, graph_ip_households holds households that export a qualifying IPv4, and covered_ids is the set of hash values that resolve to such an IP. CRM email and phone uploads are unioned (with a source_type tag) into crm_inputs, and a single GROUP BY computes both metric pairs via conditional aggregation. Match join is on hash value alone (no id_type constraint) to be robust to upstream id mislabeling. Match rates deliberately count only pre_hash_case = LOWERCASE email rows.

    2. com.olympics.nbcu site excluded (matches CoreDW filter)
    3. Static layer: 30-day weighted history from archives fills in publishers absent
       from the 3-day dynamic window (CoreDW equivalent of publisher_adsize_metrics_static)
  Use this to validate CoreDW parity before promoting to replace summarydata.publisher_adsize_metrics.
